answer:
The file `/home/hyoklee/cae_test_data/porotomo/dasv_native_PoroTomo_iDAS025_160318160317.h5` contains **8 datasets, all at the root group (no subgroups)**. I opened it read-only, ran `hdf5_analyze_dataset_structure` on `/` (which reads shapes/dtypes from the file itself), and confirmed the root keys with `hdf5_list_keys`:

| Dataset | Shape | Dtype |
|---|---|---|
| `das` | (30000, 384) | float32 |
| `t` | (30000,) | float64 |
| `trace` | (30000,) | int64 |
| `x` | (384,) | float32 |
| `y` | (384,) | float32 |
| `z` | (384,) | float32 |
| `channel` | (384,) | int32 |
| `crs` | () (scalar) | uint8 |

Notes on what this means for the PoroTomo data:
- `das` is the main DAS strain-rate array: 30,000 time samples × 384 channels (float32).
- `t` (float64) is the per-sample time axis, `trace` (int64) the trace numbering, and `x`/`y`/`z` the per-channel spatial coordinates along the fiber; `channel` indexes the 384 channels and `crs` is a scalar coordinate-reference-system flag.
- The filename encodes instrument `iDAS025` and a start stamp of 2016-03-18 16:03:17, consistent with the March 2016 Brady Hot Springs experiment.

One caveat: root/dataset attribute listing failed through the HDF5 tool (`Object of type bytes/ndarray is not JSON serializable`), so any unit/label attributes stored on these objects were not readable this way — the shapes and dtypes above, however, were read directly from the file and cross-checked with the key listing.
